citation: Bancroft, Hubert Howe. The Book of the Fair: An Historical and Descriptive Presentation of the World's Science, Art, and Industry, as Viewed through the Columbian Exposition at Chicago in 1893. Vol. 1. Chicago: The Bancroft Company, 1893.
author: Hubert Howe Bancroft
repository: Internet Archive, from the Smithsonian Libraries copy
locator: Scan leaf 76: 'The reasons for painting the buildings white, thus giving to the Fair its appellation of White City, Mr Millet explains ...'.
rights_note: Published 1893 in the United States; the Internet Archive record marks it public domain.
access_notes: Read 2026-10-16 (T-2611) through the Internet Archive's full-text search of this scan, at the leaf the locator names; the page images were not opened.
note: Published in the year of the fair, so period evidence for it. Used for one time-stream caption on the way to 1812 and 1835 (the year 1893): that the fair's buildings were painted white and the fair was called the White City. Nothing in any scene is built from it.
what_it_supplies: that the Columbian Exposition's buildings were painted white, which gave the fair the name White City
